content_voiceover: This is step one of the practical VWD diagnostic algorithm, is VWF activity low. It tests platelet-dependent VWF activity together with VWF antigen. Activity clearly above one hundred international units per deciliter is not consistent with VWD. Activity between fifty and one hundred requires asking whether the sample was drawn during a period of wellness, since VWF is an acute phase reactant that rises with stress, inflammation, pregnancy, or estrogen; if the sample was drawn during illness, you retest at baseline before concluding anything. Activity between thirty and fifty is labeled low VWF, sometimes mild type 1. Activity below thirty international units per deciliter is more classic for type 1 or type 2 VWD. The key exam point is that VWF is an acute phase reactant, and blood type O individuals run roughly twenty five to thirty percent lower baseline levels than non-O, both of which matter when interpreting a borderline result.
keypoints: VWF activity >100 IU/dL: not consistent with VWD
50-100 IU/dL: check if drawn during wellness; if not, retest at baseline
<30 IU/dL: classic type 1 or type 2 VWD
VWF is an acute-phase reactant; blood type O = ~25-30% lower baseline
keypoint_voiceover: Step one asks whether VWF activity is low. Above one hundred rules out VWD. Between fifty and one hundred, check if the sample was drawn during wellness, and retest at baseline if not. Thirty to fifty is labeled low VWF. Below thirty is classic type 1 or type 2 disease.
